tool.name: CRISPRTarget make database
tool.description: build a target database and its shuffled control database
tool.command: #if $input_fasta.is_of_type('fasta.gz') gunzip -c '$input_fasta' > input.fna && #else ln -s '$input_fasta' input.fna && #end if ## builds the BLAST database (with a samtools index) and the shuffled control database MakeUserDB.sh input.fna target_db && MakeUserShuffledDB.sh input.fna control_db && ## the databases are archived and the unpacked files are removed from the job directory ## (zip cannot write to the empty file that Galaxy creates for the output) zip -r -q target_database.zip target_db && mv target_database.zip '$target_db' && zip -r -q control_database.zip control_db && mv control_database.zip '$control_db' && rm -rf target_db control_db

param.name: input_fasta
param.label: Target sequences (e.g. phage or plasmid genomes)

tool.help:
**What it does**
This tool turns a FASTA file into a CRISPRTarget database, i.e. into
- a **target database**: a nucleotide BLAST database of the input sequences (created with ``makeblastdb -parse_seqids -blastdb_version 4``) together with a samtools index of the FASTA file, and - a **shuffled control database**: the same sequences shuffled with ``esl-shuffle``, which CRISPRTarget uses to estimate the p-values of the matches.
Both databases are returned as zip archives of the directory that contains the FASTA file, the BLAST database files and the ``.fai`` index.
-----
**Where to use the outputs**
The zip archives are the artifact that the CRISPRTarget tool needs. Hand them (or the unpacked directories) to the Galaxy administrator, who adds one line per database pair to the ``crispr_target_databases`` data table, so that the databases can be selected in the CRISPRTarget tool. See the help of the CRISPRTarget tool for details.
If you only want to run a single search, the CRISPRTarget tool can also build the databases from a FASTA file of your history on the fly, in which case this tool is not needed.
-----
**Note**
The shuffled control database is generated with a random seed, hence two runs of this tool on the same input result in different control databases. Both are equally valid, but the p-values of identical searches may differ slightly.
